additional_concerns: Paragraph 10 establishes continuing responsibility but supplies no complete test combining retained authority, effective supervision and satisfactory performance. The candidate's three-part test requires justification under an identified applicable standard.

The proper-records and operational-compatibility duties support examining actual outcomes, but the excerpts do not establish strict liability for every incident or specify materiality, duration, remediation or the assessment period. Missing facts must remain unresolved.
UT Code 6.11C expressly concerns third-party valuation. Its reasonable-care and supervision standard cannot automatically be imported into tokenisation responsibility.

Paragraph 14 and footnote 5 connect assurance to underlying compliance; confirmation, demonstration, an audit or a legal opinion does not itself establish substantive fulfillment. The request phrase directly qualifies demonstration; whether SFC satisfaction also governs confirmation remains unresolved.

Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition procurement of an audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion on SFC request. Absence of a request does not remove paragraph 10 responsibility or the independently stated confirmation duty.
Part A, the omitted requirements within paragraphs 10–13 and footnote 2 may be needed to establish the full applicable standard. No external dependency catalogue IDs are supplied.
No executable meaning or operational facts are supplied. The structural tool result and retrieval matches establish neither legal fidelity nor fulfillment.
